agenda: Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our primary objective is to mobilize Council action and reinforce targeted sanctions, border controls, and counter-terrorist financing measures against the rapidly metastasizing transnational threat of ISIL-Khorasan in the wake of the New Orleans attack and related external plots. We anticipate difficult negotiations with Russia and China regarding language pressing the Taliban on verifiable counter-terrorism commitments and references to regional security vacuums, as well as potential pushback against detailed human rights and rule-of-law conditionalities. Additionally, managing Pakistan's concerns regarding regional safe havens while ensuring European allies are satisfied with strong IHL and humanitarian safeguards will require careful drafting.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the draft resolution and reaffirms its steadfast commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. However, we believe the Council's response must not overlook the grave escalation of terrorist threats in Africa, particularly in the Sahel, nor the imperative of tackling the root causes that fuel violent extremism. We also urge the penholder to reinforce language on suppressing terrorist financing, including the critical issue of kidnapping for ransom, while ensuring capacity-building strictly respects national ownership.
messages.China: China supports international counter-terrorism cooperation and recognizes the urgent need to address the threat posed by ISIL-K and other terrorist forces. To be comprehensive and effective, the resolution must adopt a zero-tolerance approach to all terrorist groups designated by the Council, including the Eastern Turkistan Islamic Movement (ETIM/TIP), and firmly reject double standards. Furthermore, sustainable counter-terrorism in Afghanistan requires constructive engagement, addressing economic distress, and releasing Afghanistan's legitimate overseas assets rather than relying solely on pressure.
messages.Denmark: Denmark welcomes the draft resolution circulated by the United States addressing the grave and growing transnational threat posed by ISIL-Khorasan and its affiliates. We appreciate the draft's robust language on international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and gender mainstreaming. To further strengthen the text, Denmark requests an explicit operational link to resolution 2664 (2022) in paragraph 6 to protect principled humanitarian action from de-risking and CFT impediments, as well as an acknowledgement of the Ombudsperson's indispensable role in ensuring due process.
messages.France: France strongly supports the draft resolution circulated by the United States to confront the growing transnational threat posed by ISIL-Khorasan and to reinforce the 1267 sanctions architecture. To align fully with the Council's landmark achievements in resolution 2734 (2024), we request explicit reference in OP3 to designations targeting perpetrators of sexual and gender-based violence. Furthermore, the Council must remain consistent regarding Afghanistan by recalling that the fight against terrorism cannot be decoupled from the Taliban's respect for basic human rights, particularly the rights of women and girls.
messages.Greece: Greece strongly supports this timely draft resolution and commends the United States for addressing the acute and evolving transnational threat posed by ISIL-Khorasan. As a maritime nation and an external border state of the European Union, Greece emphasizes the importance of addressing vulnerabilities across all transport and border domains, including maritime routes. We look forward to working closely with the penholder and all Council members to achieve a robust text that reinforces international cooperation anchored in international law and the rule of law.
messages.Guyana: Guyana unequivocally condemns terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and welcomes the penholder's timely initiative to address the evolving transnational threat posed by ISIL-K. We believe the text would be further strengthened by explicitly acknowledging the need to address the root causes and socio-economic drivers of violent extremism. Additionally, given the technological and resource constraints faced by many developing states, it is critical that obligations regarding border security and virtual asset regulation are paired with robust, tailored capacity-building and technical assistance.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan has stood at the forefront of the global fight against terrorism and has paid the heaviest price in human lives and economic losses, particularly from attacks staged from across our western border. Any balanced resolution addressing terrorist threats emanating from Afghanistan must explicitly hold the Taliban accountable for safe havens provided to Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP)—a UN-designated group—alongside ISIL-K and Al-Qaeda. Furthermore, the text must acknowledge the grave attacks suffered by Pakistan and address the systemic root causes that fuel violent extremism.
messages.Panama: Panama welcomes and strongly supports the draft resolution introduced by the United States to counter the growing transnational threat posed by ISIL-K. As a major global maritime and logistics hub, Panama places great importance on securing global transport supply chains and dismantling the nexus between terrorist financing and transnational illicit flows. We appreciate the penholder's balanced approach and stand ready to vote in favor of this resolution.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea strongly supports the United States' timely draft resolution addressing the growing transnational threat posed by ISIL-Khorasan and associated networks. Given the sophisticated exploitation of new technologies and illicit financial channels by terrorist groups, we propose minor enhancements to strengthen provisions on virtual asset service providers and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. We stand ready to work closely with the penholder to ensure swift consensus and adoption.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation welcomes the draft's focus on the acute transnational threat posed by ISIL-Khorasan, including the explicit condemnation of the heinous terrorist attacks in Moscow, Kerman, and elsewhere. However, counter-terrorism resolutions must not be politicized through external agendas, non-consensual gender concepts, or references to politicized external bodies such as the FATF. Moreover, addressing the terrorist threat emanating from Afghanistan requires an objective acknowledgment of the situation on the ground and practical interaction with the de facto authorities in Kabul.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone strongly supports the draft resolution and commends the United States for addressing the growing transnational threat posed by ISIL-K and associated networks. In line with the Council's landmark adoption of resolution 2734 (2024), we urge the penholder to explicitly recall sexual and gender-based violence as a designated listing criterion under the sanctions regime. Additionally, we underscore the critical importance of tailoring technical assistance and capacity-building to support developing countries, particularly across the African continent, in meeting global counter-terrorism and financial standards.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the draft resolution presented by the United States and strongly supports decisive, united Council action against the evolving transnational threat posed by ISIL-Khorasan. To ensure these measures are robust and sustainable, we place paramount importance on strict adherence to international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and the rule of law, as well as the full, equal, and meaningful participation of women in counter-terrorism efforts. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder to finalize the text.
messages.Somalia: Somalia strongly welcomes the United States' initiative to tackle the escalating transnational threat posed by ISIL-K and associated terrorist networks. As a frontline state combating both Al-Shabaab and Da'esh elements, Somalia stresses the need to reflect the interconnected nature of these groups and their operational nodes across Africa. Additionally, we must ensure counter-terrorist financing measures do not inadvertently impede vital remittance lifelines upon which millions depend, while prioritizing robust capacity-building support for frontline states.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly welcomes the United States' leadership on this timely and vital draft resolution addressing the growing transnational threat posed by ISIL-K. We fully support the resolution's core objectives, including disrupting terrorist financing, travel, and emerging technology exploitation. We propose two targeted additions to reflect established international standards: ensuring border data collection aligns with ICAO frameworks and data protection rights, and reinforcing the full, equal, and meaningful participation of women in line with our shared Women, Peace, and Security commitments.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United States successfully resolved the red lines of China (explicitly designating ETIM/TIP in OP7), Pakistan (explicitly naming TTP in OP7), and the Russian Federation (deleting former OP9 on gender mainstreaming while anchoring SGBV accountability in OP3 under resolution 2734). We accommodated the key priorities of France, the United Kingdom, Denmark, Slovenia, Sierra Leone, Algeria, Somalia, ROK, Greece, Guyana, and Panama regarding humanitarian carve-outs, the Ombudsperson, FATF standards, maritime and border security, and frontline capacity-building. The revised draft preserves vital US counter-terrorism objectives while maintaining broad consensus across the entire Security Council.

messages.Algeria: Algeria extends its appreciation to the penholder for constructively incorporating our priorities into the revised text, particularly regarding the expansion of terrorist threats across Africa and the Sahel, the categorical rejection of ransom payments to terrorist groups, and the emphasis on national ownership and root causes. The draft strikes a balanced and robust approach to countering the evolving transnational terrorist threat while respecting State sovereignty and international law. Algeria is pleased to support the resolution as drafted and looks forward to its swift adoption.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder's constructive engagement in accommodating our key priorities in Revision 1, particularly the explicit references to the Eastern Turkistan Islamic Movement (ETIM/TIP), the affirmation of State sovereignty and the UN Charter, and the inclusion of agreed language on Afghanistan's Central Bank assets. The revised draft presents a balanced framework that reflects the shared resolve of the international community to combat terrorism in all its forms. China supports the adoption of the text as currently drafted and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the United States for constructively accommodating our proposals regarding humanitarian safeguards under resolution 2664 (2022) and the essential role of the Office of the Ombudsperson in guaranteeing due process and the rule of law. The current text strikes a sound balance between robust international counter-terrorism measures and strict adherence to international law, human rights, and humanitarian principles. Denmark fully supports the draft resolution as revised and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.France: France thanks the United States for accommodating our proposals in Revision 1, in particular regarding accountability for international crimes, the sanctions designation criterion on sexual and gender-based violence, and the firm demand that the Taliban respect international human rights law and rescind restrictions against women and girls. We fully support the draft text as it currently stands, which reinforces our collective counter-terrorism architecture while upholding the rule of law, human rights, and humanitarian space. France is ready to vote in favour of this resolution.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the United States for its constructive stewardship of this draft and for fully incorporating our proposals regarding maritime security and human rights compliance. The revised text provides a balanced, robust, and comprehensive framework to confront the growing transnational threat posed by ISIL-K and its affiliates while upholding the rule of law and international obligations. Greece fully supports the adoption of the resolution in its current form.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the United States for constructively engaging with our delegation and fully incorporating our proposals regarding root causes, sustainable development, and tailored capacity-building support for developing countries. The revised draft strikes a necessary and comprehensive balance between robust counter-terrorism measures, the protection of human rights, and adherence to international law. Guyana fully supports the draft resolution in its current form and looks forward to voting in favor.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan expresses its appreciation to the penholder for constructively incorporating our core concerns in Revision 1, specifically by acknowledging the recurring deadly attacks in Pakistan in preambular paragraph 4 and explicitly including Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) in operative paragraph 7. As a frontline state and principal victim of transnational terrorism, Pakistan attaches the highest importance to robust international cooperation and an uncompromising stance against all terrorist groups, including TTP and ISIL-K. We are satisfied with the balanced text as currently formulated and are prepared to vote in favour of the draft resolution.
messages.Panama: Panama commends the United States delegation for its leadership and appreciates the constructive inclusion of our priorities regarding maritime security and the interdiction of illicit trafficking networks in operative paragraph 10. The revised draft strikes a comprehensive balance between robust counter-terrorism measures, the suppression of terrorist financing, and full adherence to international law and human rights standards. Panama is pleased to fully support this draft resolution as it moves forward to adoption.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea commends the United States for steering these negotiations and warmly welcomes the inclusion of our proposals on virtual asset regulation, FATF standards, and artificial intelligence in revision 1. The draft presents a robust, balanced, and timely response to the evolving transnational threat posed by ISIL-K and associated groups while safeguarding international legal standards and financial integrity. We stand ready to vote in favor of the resolution as drafted.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation notes that despite the penholder's indication, OP9 remains in the circulated text; its complete deletion is our firm red line, as the Monitoring Team's reporting cycle is already well-regulated and should not be burdened with extraneous ad hoc mandates. Additionally, the Security Council must avoid attempting to artificially expand the 1267 sanctions regime or re-litigate contentious elements from resolution 2734, on which we abstained. If our red line on OP9 is genuinely resolved, Russia is prepared to support the resolution.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the United States for constructively engaging with our delegation and incorporating our priorities into Revision 1, specifically regarding the designated listing criterion on sexual and gender-based violence and tailored technical assistance for developing countries in Africa. The draft strikes a robust and balanced approach to addressing the evolving transnational threat of terrorism while upholding international law, human rights, and humanitarian carve-outs. Sierra Leone fully supports the text as currently drafted and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the United States for constructively accommodating our proposals in this revision, particularly regarding the reinforcement of international human rights and privacy safeguards in digital counter-terrorism efforts and the protection of principled humanitarian action. The current draft presents a robust, balanced, and comprehensive framework that effectively tackles the threat posed by ISIL-K and its affiliates while strictly upholding international law, human rights, and the rule of law. Slovenia is ready to support the text as drafted.
messages.Somalia: Somalia commends the United States for its constructive engagement and for incorporating our key priorities in Revision 1. We welcome the explicit recognition of the threats posed by Al-Shabaab and Da'esh affiliates, the vital protection of legitimate diaspora remittances and financial inclusion, and the emphasis on targeted capacity-building for frontline African states. Somalia fully supports this balanced and robust draft resolution and is prepared to vote in favor.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the United States for its constructive engagement and for accommodating our priorities in Revision 1, particularly the integration of ICAO standards, robust human rights safeguards, and privacy protections into operative paragraph 5. The draft strikes the necessary balance between resolute, collective action against the evolving transnational threat posed by ISIL-K and adherence to international law, human rights, and humanitarian carve-outs. We fully support the resolution as currently drafted and look forward to its prompt adoption.

steps.summary: To avert a veto and achieve consensus, the penholder fully accommodated the Russian Federation's firm red line by deleting former operative paragraph 9 on the ad hoc Monitoring Team reporting mandate. Essential counter-terrorism priorities, including the landmark sanctions designation criterion on sexual and gender-based violence and standard Financial Action Task Force references, were successfully preserved in alignment with the overwhelming majority of Council members. With all member priorities reconciled, the resolution enjoys unanimous support across the Security Council.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria has consistently supported robust multilateral counter-terrorism frameworks under the 1267/1989/2253 regime, and the draft appropriately reflects key national priorities, including addressing root causes, prohibiting ransom payments, and supporting capacity-building for African states.
reasons.China: China supports the draft resolution as it bolsters international counter-terrorism cooperation, explicitly addresses groups threatening Chinese and regional security such as the Eastern Turkistan Islamic Movement (ETIM), and reflects key priorities regarding state sovereignty, addressing root causes, and economic support for Afghanistan. In line with its standard practice on counter-terrorism adoptions, China will vote in favour and deliver any remarks after the vote.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the draft resolution, which strengthens multilateral counter-terrorism efforts against ISIL-K and other terrorist groups while reinforcing international human rights law, due process via the Ombudsperson, and humanitarian safeguards under resolution 2664 (2022).
reasons.France: France fully supports the draft resolution, which strengthens the international framework against Da’esh/ISIL-K and Al-Qaeda, reinforces sanctions implementation, integrates accountability for sexual and gender-based violence, and upholds international human rights and humanitarian law.
reasons.Greece: Greece fully supports the draft resolution, which strengthens multilateral counter-terrorism efforts against ISIL-K and other terrorist groups while upholding international law, human rights, and border security. Having endorsed the text during negotiations, Greece votes in favour without delivering a statement before the vote.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft resolution as it reinforces international counter-terrorism cooperation, addresses the growing threat of ISIL-K and other terrorist networks, and properly upholds international human rights law and humanitarian carve-outs.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan fully supports the draft resolution as it explicitly addresses the grave threat posed by ISIL-K and demands that the Afghan authorities sever ties with and take verifiable action against terrorist entities, including Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which routinely carry out attacks against Pakistan. Consistent with Council practice, Pakistan votes in favour and reserves its remarks for the explanation of vote following the adoption.
reasons.Panama: Panama consistently supports multilateral counter-terrorism efforts, robust sanctions implementation, and international law compliance, and explicitly endorsed the draft text during negotiations.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea consistently supports robust international counter-terrorism frameworks and aligned fully with the draft text sponsored by the United States, which addresses critical threats including ISIL-K and terrorist exploitation of new technologies.
reasons.Russian Federation: With our red line on the deletion of paragraph 9 accommodated by the penholder, the Russian Federation can support the draft resolution. Combating ISIL-K, which claimed responsibility for the heinous Crocus City Hall attack in Moscow and continues to threaten regional stability across Eurasia, remains a vital national security priority. While we maintain reservations regarding certain non-consensus concepts, including references to SGBV listing criteria and external FATF standards, our primary concerns were addressed.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone fully supports the draft resolution as it reinforces the international counter-terrorism framework, incorporates capacity-building for African states, references FATF standards and humanitarian carve-outs, and upholds the listing criterion on sexual and gender-based violence.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the draft resolution as it reinforces multilateral counter-terrorism efforts against ISIL-K and other affiliates while safeguarding international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and the humanitarian carve-outs established under resolution 2664 (2022).
reasons.Somalia: As a frontline state battling Al-Shabaab and ISIL affiliates, Somalia strongly supports multilateral counter-terrorism cooperation, sanctions implementation, and capacity-building assistance, and thus votes in favour of the resolution.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports this US-drafted resolution, which reinforces international counter-terrorism architecture against ISIL-K and associated groups, upholds the 1267/1989 sanctions regime, enhances border security tools like API/PNR, and ensures counter-terrorism efforts adhere to international human rights standards.
reasons.United States of America: As the penholder and sponsor of the draft resolution, the United States fully supports the text, which reflects core U.S. counter-terrorism priorities, strengthens the 1267 sanctions regime against ISIS-K, and addresses terrorist financing and human rights. Delivering an introductory statement before the vote underscores U.S. leadership and rallies Council support.

before.Somalia:
Mr. President,

Somalia votes in favour of this draft resolution. As a nation on the frontlines of the global fight against terrorism, Somalia understands firsthand the devastating impact of violent extremism, including the threats posed by Al-Shabaab and Da’esh affiliates to innocent civilians, regional stability, and national development. 

International terrorism recognizes no borders. Disrupting the transnational operational reach, illicit financing corridors, and recruitment networks of groups like ISIL-K and Al-Qaeda requires resolute collective action, enhanced intelligence-sharing, and meaningful technical assistance and capacity-building for frontline states. 

We welcome the draft resolution’s balanced approach, including its emphasis on border security, addressing the conditions conducive to terrorism, safeguarding legitimate diaspora remittances and humanitarian action, and upholding national sovereignty and international law. Somalia remains steadfast in its commitment to eradicating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and urges the Council to adopt this resolution unanimously.

Thank you.
before.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

As the penholder of today’s draft resolution, the United States is proud to put forward this vital measure, which directly confronts the evolving, highly adaptable, and deadly threat posed by international terrorism—in particular, the alarming transnational resurgence of ISIS-Khorasan and affiliated networks across South and Central Asia, the Middle East, and the African continent.

The devastating attacks in New Orleans, Moscow, Kerman, and throughout Pakistan serve as a tragic reminder that terrorist groups respect no borders, no religions, and no humanity. ISIS-K has demonstrated a clear intent and increasing operational capacity to project violence far beyond its historical core, exploiting regional instability, porous borders, and emerging technologies—from virtual assets to encrypted digital platforms—to recruit, finance, and execute mass-casualty attacks.

This resolution takes robust, concrete action under Chapter VII. It reaffirms and strengthens the implementation of the 1267/1989/2253 sanctions architecture and urges Member States to actively target ISIS-K facilitation and external operations networks. It establishes practical expectations for tightening border security through API/PNR standards and combating illicit financing in line with Financial Action Task Force standards, while upholding the cross-cutting humanitarian carve-out established in resolution 2664. Crucially, the text maintains our unwavering demand that the Taliban strictly adhere to their counter-terrorism commitments, sever ties with all terrorist groups, and immediately rescind the oppressive decrees violating the human rights and fundamental freedoms of Afghan women and girls. Furthermore, it reinforces our landmark recognition in resolution 2734 that sexual and gender-based violence is a deliberate tactic of terror that must be met with full accountability.

Throughout consultations, the United States listened carefully to all Council members to forge a balanced, comprehensive, and action-oriented text that delivers critical technical capacity to frontline States while strictly upholding international law, human rights, and the rule of law. We urge all Council members to vote in favor of this resolution and send an unmistakable, unified message: this Council will not permit safe havens for terrorists, and we remain resolute in protecting international peace and security.

Thank you.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. Our vote reflects our steadfast conviction that terrorism in all its forms and manifestations remains one of the gravest threats to international peace and security, requiring an uncompromising, unified, and coordinated global response. 

Having endured and overcome the horrors of a devastating decade of terrorism through immense national sacrifice and resilience, Algeria approaches counter-terrorism not merely as a matter of security, but as an existential imperative. We reiterate our unequivocal condemnation of all acts of terrorism, wherever, whenever, and by whomsoever committed. Terrorism cannot and must not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization, or ethnic group.

The resolution adopted today rightly sounds the alarm on the expanding transnational reach and lethality of Da’esh, Al-Qaeda, and their affiliates, including ISIL-Khorasan. At the same time, my delegation emphasizes the acute and growing threat posed by these terrorist networks across the African continent, particularly in the Sahel, the Lake Chad basin, and parts of East and Southern Africa. African nations are bearing an unbearable burden on the frontlines of this global scourge. The international community cannot afford selective vigilance; combating terrorism requires sustained, predictable, and adequate support for African-led initiatives, coupled with genuine capacity-building and intelligence cooperation.

Military and security responses, while necessary, are insufficient on their own to achieve lasting success. Counter-terrorism strategies must address the root causes and underlying conditions conducive to the spread of terrorism, including persistent poverty, underdevelopment, youth unemployment, the adverse effects of climate change, and the absence of state authority. 

Furthermore, all counter-terrorism operations and measures must strictly comply with the Charter of the United Nations, international law, international humanitarian law, and international human rights law, with full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of affected States. We welcome the reaffirmation in this resolution of the humanitarian carve-outs established by resolution 2664 (2022), which are essential to ensure that principled humanitarian action is never impeded.

Finally, Algeria reaffirms the central importance of preserving the integrity, credibility, and Member State-driven nature of United Nations sanctions regimes, including the 1267 Committee. We must guard against any politicization of sanctions mechanisms, continue to strengthen the Office of the Ombudsperson to guarantee fair and clear procedures and due process, and ensure that our collective efforts remain firmly rooted in consensus and international solidarity.

I thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. 

Terrorism is the common enemy of all humanity. At present, the international counter-terrorism situation remains complex and grim. Terrorist organizations, including Da’esh, Al-Qaida, and their regional affiliates—most notably ISIL-Khorasan—are exploiting regional instability and new technologies to step up recruitment, financing, and cross-border attacks, posing a severe threat to international and regional peace and security. Today’s resolution once again demonstrates the unified resolve of the international community to combat all forms of terrorism.

China wishes to emphasize the following points:

First, we must adhere to a unified standard and zero tolerance in combating terrorism. There is no such thing as "good" or "bad" terrorists. All terrorist forces designated by the Security Council—including ISIL, Al-Qaida, the Eastern Turkistan Islamic Movement (ETIM), and others—must be resolutely and unequivocally combated without double standards or selective approaches. Counter-terrorism should not be politicized or instrumentalized, nor should it be linked to any particular country, ethnicity, or religion.

Second, the central coordinating role of the United Nations in international counter-terrorism efforts must be fully leveraged. All counter-terrorism operations must strictly abide by the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, respect the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of the countries concerned, and adhere to international law. The Security Council sanctions regimes are vital instruments, and we support their effective and objective implementation, while ensuring due process and avoiding adverse impacts on legitimate economic and humanitarian activities.

Third, we must address both the symptoms and root causes of terrorism. Military and security measures alone cannot eradicate the soil in which terrorism breeds. The international community should help developing countries, particularly frontline states in Africa and Asia, to strengthen their counter-terrorism capacities, promote sustainable development, eradicate poverty, and foster dialogue and social cohesion.

Finally, regarding the situation in Afghanistan, China urges the Afghan interim authorities to take sustained and verifiable measures to fulfill their counter-terrorism commitments, and resolutely prevent Afghan territory from being used to harbor terrorist groups or threaten neighboring countries. At the same time, the international community should maintain constructive engagement with the Afghan interim administration and assist Afghanistan in overcoming its economic and humanitarian challenges. We once again urge the countries concerned to immediately and unconditionally unfreeze and return in full the overseas assets belonging to the Afghan Central Bank and lift all illegal unilateral sanctions, so as to create conditions for Afghanistan's peaceful reconstruction and the fundamental elimination of the terrorist threat.

China stands ready to continue working with all members of the international community to safeguard international peace and security.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Denmark:
Mr. President,

Denmark voted in favour of the resolution adopted today, and we thank the United States for its leadership as penholder.

Today’s unanimous adoption sends a clear, united, and necessary message: the international community stands firmly together against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. The alarming transnational reach and adaptability of ISIL-Khorasan, as well as the persistence of Al-Qaeda and associated affiliates across Central and South Asia, the Middle East, and large parts of the African continent, demand our collective and resolute action.

For Denmark, an effective response to terrorism requires that we remain steadfast in upholding our shared values and legal obligations. We welcome that the resolution explicitly reaffirms that all counter-terrorism measures must strictly comply with international law, including the UN Charter, international human rights law, international refugee law, and international humanitarian law. Human rights, fundamental freedoms, and the rule of law are not obstacles to security; they are the bedrock of sustainable peace and the most effective defense against violent extremism.

We also welcome the resolution’s strong emphasis on fair and clear procedures, including the vital role of the Office of the Ombudsperson, as well as its reaffirmation of resolution 2664 (2022) to safeguard impartial humanitarian action and principled aid delivery. 

Furthermore, Denmark underscores the critical importance of integrating the Women, Peace, and Security agenda into all counter-terrorism efforts. We strongly support the resolution's recognition of conflict-related sexual violence as a tactic of terrorism and its call for full accountability for perpetrators, as well as the meaningful participation and leadership of women in preventing and countering violent extremism.

To sustainably defeat terrorism, we must also address the conditions conducive to its spread, including through promoting good governance, sustainable development, and social cohesion, while countering the exploitation of new technologies for radicalization and recruitment.

Denmark remains fully committed to working with the Security Council and international partners to combat terrorism effectively, lawfully, and comprehensively.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
Monsieur le Président,

France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution, which reaffirms the Security Council's unity and determination in the face of the evolving threat posed by international terrorism. We thank the United States for its initiative and for steering the negotiations to a successful conclusion.

The menace posed by Da’esh, Al-Qaida, and their regional affiliates—most notably Da’esh-Khorasan—remains acute and deeply concerning. The tragic attacks in New Orleans, Moscow, Kerman, and across Pakistan, as well as the foiled plots against public events, demonstrate that these terrorist groups retain the intent and the operational capability to strike far beyond their traditional bases. We also remain particularly alarmed by the expanding footprint and lethality of terrorist groups across the African continent, particularly in the Sahel and the Lake Chad basin, where local populations bear the heaviest toll of extremist violence.

In the face of these transnational threats, our collective response must remain resolute and comprehensive. France fully supports the strict implementation of the targeted sanctions regime established under resolutions 1267, 1989, and 2253, and we emphasize the indispensable role of the Office of the Ombudsperson in safeguarding due process and the rule of law. We must also redouble our efforts to disrupt terrorist financing, counter online radicalization, and prevent the misuse of emerging technologies, such as unmanned aerial systems and artificial intelligence.

France particularly welcomes the text’s strong reaffirmation that sexual and gender-based violence is used as a deliberate tactic of terrorism by Da’esh and other groups to terrorize populations, subjugate women and girls, and generate illicit resources. There can be no sustainable peace without justice, and those responsible for these heinous crimes must be held accountable.

Finally, France reiterates that the fight against terrorism can only succeed if it strictly respects the rule of law, international human rights law, and international humanitarian law. Human rights and effective counter-terrorism are not mutually exclusive; they are mutually reinforcing. Likewise, counter-terrorism measures must never impede principled, impartial humanitarian action.

France will continue to stand alongside its international partners, fully mobilized in the global fight against terrorism in all its forms.

Je vous remercie.
after.Greece:
Mr. President,

Greece welcomed the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution and voted in favour of this important text. 

Terrorism in all its forms and manifestations remains one of the most severe threats to international peace and security. The deadly attacks and thwarted plots across the globe—orchestrated or inspired by ISIL-Khorasan, Al-Qaeda, and their affiliates—demonstrate with alarming clarity that no region is immune to this transnational scourge. Greece extends its heartfelt condolences to all victims of terrorism and their families.

Today’s unanimous vote reaffirms the Council’s united resolve to confront this threat through effective multilateral cooperation. For Greece, an effective counter-terrorism strategy rests on three fundamental pillars:

First, counter-terrorism operations must strictly adhere to the Charter of the United Nations and international law, including international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and international refugee law. Counter-terrorism measures and the protection of human rights are not mutually exclusive; they are complementary and mutually reinforcing. Preserving principled humanitarian action, in line with resolution 2664 (2022), remains equally essential.

Second, we must adapt to the evolving tactics of terrorist networks. This includes disrupting their illicit financial flows, curbing the exploitation of emerging technologies—such as unmanned aerial systems, artificial intelligence, and virtual assets—and addressing the link between terrorism, transnational organized crime, and maritime security.

Third, long-term security cannot be achieved without addressing the root causes and conditions conducive to the spread of terrorism, including prolonged conflicts, institutional fragility, and lack of socio-economic opportunities, while fully ensuring the meaningful participation of women and youth in prevention efforts.

Greece remains fully committed to working with all partners and within the United Nations framework to uphold the rule of law and defeat terrorism in all its forms.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Guyana:
Mr. President,

Guyana voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which reaffirms the collective resolve of the Security Council to confront the scourge of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. 

Terrorism continues to pose a profound threat to international peace and security, undermining state stability, destroying human lives, and stalling sustainable development. The tragic attacks cited in the resolution—including those perpetrated and inspired by ISIL-K and other terrorist entities—demonstrate the evolving and transnational nature of this threat, as well as the urgent need for robust, coordinated multilateral cooperation to counter it.

Guyana reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, committed by whomever, wherever, and for whatever purposes. We stress that terrorism cannot and should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization, or ethnic group.

In our collective efforts to combat terrorism, Guyana underscores three fundamental imperatives. 

First, all counter-terrorism measures must strictly adhere to the Charter of the United Nations and international law, including international human rights law, international refugee law, and international humanitarian law. Respect for human rights and the rule of law are not impediments to fighting terrorism; rather, they are indispensable to its success and long-term sustainability.

Second, an effective counter-terrorism strategy must address the root causes and conditions conducive to the spread of terrorism and violent extremism. Security measures alone will not suffice. We must address poverty, social and economic inequality, lack of opportunity, and governance deficits, while investing in sustainable development, social cohesion, and the empowerment of women and youth.

Third, Guyana welcomes the resolution’s reaffirmation of the critical humanitarian carve-outs established under resolution 2664 (2022). It is essential that sanctions regimes and counter-terrorism financing frameworks do not inadvertently impede the delivery of impartial, principled humanitarian assistance to vulnerable populations in need.

Guyana remains committed to working with all Council members and the wider international community to strengthen international cooperation, uphold the international legal architecture, and build a more peaceful and secure world.

I thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. 

As a country on the front lines of the global fight against terrorism, Pakistan has borne an immense burden. We have suffered tens of thousands of casualties—both civilian and security personnel—and incurred economic losses exceeding hundreds of billions of dollars. No nation has sacrificed more, nor has any nation been more steadfast in its resolve to eliminate the scourge of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.

We welcome the Council’s united condemnation of the heinous terrorist attacks orchestrated and inspired by ISIL-K (Da’esh-Khorasan), which has demonstrated an alarming transnational reach, striking innocent civilians from Moscow to Kerman, New Orleans, and repeatedly within Pakistan. 

However, as we confront the lethal menace of ISIL-K, the international community must not lose sight of other major terrorist entities that threaten regional peace and stability. For Pakistan, a grave and persistent threat emanates from the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP)—or *Fitna al-Khawarij*—as well as associated terrorist syndicates like the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its Majeed Brigade. These groups continue to find safe havens across our western border, from where they recruit, plan, and conduct cross-border attacks against our security forces, civilians, and critical infrastructure, including foreign nationals working on development projects.

In this context, we reiterate the Council’s categorical demand that the territory of Afghanistan must not be used as a base, staging ground, or safe haven to threaten or attack any country, or to shelter and train terrorists. We call upon the Afghan interim authorities to fulfill their explicit counter-terrorism obligations and take verifiable, sustained, and decisive action to neutralize all terrorist organizations operating from within Afghan territory. At the same time, we stress the importance of constructive engagement with Afghanistan, including addressing its humanitarian needs and unfreezing its national assets to alleviate the suffering of the Afghan people.

Mr. President,

A comprehensive and sustainable counter-terrorism strategy requires confronting the phenomenon holistically. First, we must address the root causes and underlying conditions conducive to terrorism, including foreign occupation, protracted unresolved conflicts, poverty, disenfranchisement, and injustice. 

Second, the international community must maintain a clear distinction between acts of terrorism and the legitimate, internationally recognized struggle of peoples under foreign occupation for their right to self-determination, as enshrined in the United Nations Charter and international law.

Third, terrorism must never be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization, or ethnic group. We must firmly reject the rising tide of Islamophobia, xenophobia, and right-wing violent extremism that targets Muslim communities globally. 

Finally, selective approaches and double standards in combating terrorism must end. State-sponsored terrorism, cross-border subversion, and the financing of hostile proxies against sovereign states must be condemned and dismantled with equal vigor.

Pakistan remains fully committed to collaborating with regional and international partners, and with this Council, to defeat terrorism in all its manifestations and to ensure durable peace and security for our people and the world.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Panama:
Mr. President,

Panama voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, reaffirming our steadfast commitment to the multilateral framework and our categorical condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, regardless of where, when, or by whomsoever committed. Terrorism constitutes one of the most serious threats to international peace and security, democracy, and human dignity, and it cannot and must not be associated with any religion, nationality, or ethnic group.

The growing transnational reach, adaptability, and operational lethality of ISIL-K and other terrorist networks—demonstrated by tragic attacks against innocent civilians in diverse regions across the globe—demand a unified, coordinated, and resolute international response. We must redouble our collective efforts to dismantle their recruitment pipelines, disrupt their transnational logistical corridors, and counter the exploitation of new and emerging technologies, including digital platforms and virtual assets.

As an international logistics, maritime, and financial hub, Panama places paramount importance on strengthening international cooperation to cut off the illicit financing of terrorism and prevent the abuse of global financial and transportation systems by criminal and terrorist entities. 

At the same time, Panama firmly believes that the fight against terrorism can only be sustainable and legitimate when conducted with strict adherence to international law, including international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and international refugee law. Security and the promotion of human rights are not mutually exclusive; rather, they are inherently complementary and mutually reinforcing. In this regard, we welcome the explicit recognition of the need to preserve impartial humanitarian action and the humanitarian carve-outs established by resolution 2664 (2022).

Finally, we commend the United States as penholder for its leadership and efforts to build consensus, allowing the Council to demonstrate today its unity and resolve in the global fight against terrorism.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Republic of Korea:
Mr. President,

The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, and we thank the United States for its leadership as penholder in steering these consultations to a unanimous outcome.

Today’s unanimous adoption sends a clear, united, and unequivocal message: the international community will not tolerate terrorism in any form or manifestation, wherever, whenever, and by whomsoever committed. 

The alarming resurgence and transnational projection of ISIL-Khorasan and other affiliates of Da’esh and Al-Qaeda represent a grave threat to international peace and security. Recent tragic attacks across multiple regions, targeting innocent civilians and public spaces, demonstrate that these networks continue to exploit regional instability, security vacuums, and porous borders to plan and carry out cross-border violence. We reiterate our categorical demand that the territory of Afghanistan must never be used as a base or safe haven to recruit, train, finance, or launch attacks against any country.

My delegation particularly welcomes the resolution’s timely focus on the evolving methods of terrorist financing and recruitment, notably the exploitation of new and emerging technologies, including virtual assets, artificial intelligence, encrypted platforms, and unmanned aircraft systems. As these technologies evolve rapidly, the Security Council and the wider multilateral framework must continuously strengthen our collective regulatory, intelligence-sharing, and capacity-building tools to stay ahead of malicious actors.

At the same time, the Republic of Korea firmly believes that effective counter-terrorism and the respect for the rule of law, international humanitarian law, and international human rights law are mutually reinforcing. Sanctions measures under the 1267 regime remain among our most potent multilateral instruments, and their effectiveness relies on robust implementation by all Member States, full support for the Monitoring Team, and the preservation of due process through the Office of the Ombudsperson.

In closing, Mr. President, the Republic of Korea reaffirms its steadfast commitment to working closely with all Council members and the international community to prevent and counter terrorism in all its dimensions.

I thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution submitted by the United States. 

Our position of principle is well known: terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, is an absolute evil that must be combated resolutely, uncompromisingly, and without double standards or hidden geopolitical agendas. 

Today’s resolution addresses the growing, lethal threat posed by international terrorist organizations, first and foremost the transnational resurgence and operational expansion of ISIL-Khorasan and its network of affiliates. The monstrous terrorist attack at Crocus City Hall in Moscow in March 2024, alongside the deadly attacks in Kerman, New Orleans, and recurring violence across Pakistan, graphically demonstrated that ISIL-K poses a grave threat to international peace and security and that no state is immune. We express our gratitude to Council members for demonstrating unity in condemning these heinous crimes and in paying tribute to all victims of terrorism.

At the same time, an effective response to terrorism requires genuine, coordinated international cooperation rooted in international law, respect for the sovereignty of States, and the central coordinating role of the United Nations. Counter-terrorism efforts must not be instrumentalized as a tool of political pressure or geopolitical engineering. 

In this context, we emphasize that sustainable security in Afghanistan and Central Asia cannot be achieved in isolation from the reality on the ground. Combating ISIL-K effectively requires practical, pragmatic engagement with the de facto authorities in Kabul, who are carrying out the fight against Da'esh on the frontlines. Attempts to politically isolate Afghanistan or to obstruct its economic recovery only create fertile ground for terrorist recruitment and instability. In this regard, we welcome the resolution's reaffirmation of the urgent need to address Afghanistan’s severe economic challenges, including through the unfreezing and unconditional return of Afghanistan’s national reserves for the benefit of the Afghan people.

Russia will continue to actively contribute to multilateral counter-terrorism efforts, both within the United Nations and through regional formats such as the CSTO, the SCO, and the Moscow format of consultations on Afghanistan, to eradicate the terrorist menace once and for all.

Thank you.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

Sierra Leone voted in favour of the resolution just adopted and welcomes its unanimous adoption by the Security Council. We commend the delegation of the United States, as penholder, for its leadership and constructive engagement throughout the negotiation process.

Terrorism in all its forms and manifestations remains one of the most severe threats to international peace and security. Sierra Leone unequivocally condemns all terrorist acts, wherever, whenever, and by whomsoever committed. The increasing operational capacity and transnational reach of ISIL-K, Al-Qaeda, and their affiliates—demonstrated by tragic attacks across various regions—underscore the imperative of unified, sustained, and resolute global action.

We remain particularly alarmed by the expanding footprint and lethality of terrorist networks across the African continent, most notably in the Sahel and the Lake Chad Basin. Disrupting these networks requires not only robust security responses and enhanced intelligence-sharing, but also dedicated capacity-building and technical assistance for frontline states.

Sierra Leone welcomes the resolution’s strong emphasis on combating the financing of terrorism. We reiterate our firm belief that compliance with international standards established by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is essential to choking off illicit financial flows, including the exploitation of new and emerging technologies, virtual assets, and illegal exploitation of natural resources.

Equally, we welcome the reaffirmation that conflict-related sexual violence and sexual and gender-based violence are deployed as deliberate tactics of terrorism, and we emphasize that perpetrators must be held to account. We also underscore the indispensable role of women in the prevention and resolution of conflicts and in counter-terrorism strategies.

Finally, Sierra Leone reiterates that counter-terrorism efforts can only be effective and sustainable if they strictly adhere to the Charter of the United Nations, international human rights law, international refugee law, and international humanitarian law. We must continue to safeguard impartial humanitarian action in accordance with resolution 2664 (2022), while simultaneously addressing the root causes and conditions conducive to violent extremism, including poverty, underdevelopment, and institutional fragility.

Sierra Leone reaffirms its steadfast commitment to working with the Council and the wider international community in the collective fight against terrorism.

I thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Slovenia welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution and thanks the United States as penholder for its constructive engagement throughout the negotiation process. 

Slovenia condemns terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, regardless of its motivation, wherever, whenever, and by whomsoever committed. The alarming transnational operational reach of ISIL-Khorasan and the continued threat posed by Al-Qaeda and their affiliates across South and Central Asia, the Middle East, and Africa demand a unified and decisive international response. Today’s unanimous vote demonstrates the Council’s collective resolve to counter these threats.

At the same time, Slovenia wishes to underscore three key principles that must guide our collective efforts.

First, counter-terrorism measures and the protection of human rights and the rule of law are not contradictory; they are complementary and mutually reinforcing. Any measures taken to combat terrorism must strictly comply with all obligations under international law, in particular international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and international refugee law. Counter-terrorism efforts that violate fundamental freedoms are not only unlawful, but they also risk fueling the very grievances that terrorists exploit.

Second, we welcome the resolution's reaffirmation of the need to preserve principled, impartial humanitarian action. The cross-cutting humanitarian carve-out established in resolution 2664 (2022) must be fully respected and implemented to ensure that life-saving humanitarian assistance reaches vulnerable civilian populations without obstruction or criminalization.

Third, we emphasize the critical role of fair and clear procedures and due process in UN sanctions regimes. In this regard, we continue to strongly support the Office of the Ombudsperson to the ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaeda Sanctions Committee as an essential safeguard for the legitimacy and credibility of Council sanctions.

Finally, a sustainable response to terrorism requires addressing the conditions conducive to its spread, including through good governance, sustainable development, the prevention of prolonged conflicts, and the full implementation of the Women, Peace and Security agenda. Accountability for conflict-related sexual violence used as a tactic of terrorism, alongside the meaningful participation of women in preventing violent extremism, remains indispensable.

Slovenia remains firmly committed to international cooperation against terrorism within the framework of the United Nations and the international rules-based order.

I thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution, and we thank the United States for its leadership as penholder on this critical text.

The unanimous support demonstrated by this Council today sends an unequivocal message: the international community stands united and resolute in confronting the scourge of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. 

The threats we face are increasingly dynamic, decentralized, and transnational. The deadly attacks orchestrated, directed, or inspired by ISIL-K—from Moscow and Kerman to New Orleans, alongside persistent violence across Pakistan and the wider region—underscore the urgent need for enhanced vigilance, collective action, and robust intelligence- and information-sharing. We must remain just as focused on preventing terrorist networks from exploiting security vacuums, porous borders, and new and emerging technologies, including unmanned aircraft systems and virtual assets, to radicalize, finance, and execute their heinous plots.

At the same time, this resolution rightly emphasizes that effective counter-terrorism measures and the protection of human rights, fundamental freedoms, and the rule of law are not in opposition; they are complementary and mutually reinforcing. Any counter-terrorism actions must strictly adhere to international law, including international human rights law, international refugee law, and international humanitarian law. In this regard, we welcome the resolution's reaffirmation of humanitarian carve-outs in line with resolution 2664 (2022) to ensure that vital, life-saving aid reaches civilians in need without impediment.

We also reiterate our categorical demand that Afghanistan must never again become a safe haven for international terrorists to train, plan, or project violence against any nation. The Taliban must match their rhetoric with sustained, verifiable action against all terrorist entities operating on Afghan soil. A truly secure and stable Afghanistan also requires respect for the basic human rights and fundamental freedoms of all Afghans, particularly the rights of women and girls, whose systematic exclusion from public life continues to undermine the prospects for sustainable peace.

The United Kingdom remains steadfast in its commitment to supporting the United Nations counter-terrorism architecture and working closely with our international partners to defeat terrorism and protect global security.

Thank you, Mr. President.
